one_sentence_story: Documented by Gary Goldberg in 1981 and mapped into Frontal vs Callosal circuits by Todd Feinberg in 1992, Alien (Anarchic) Hand Syndrome occurs when stroke or callosal damage breaks the brain's motor veto or interhemispheric link — unleashing smooth, unintended actions like one hand unbuttoning what the other hand just buttoned.
so_what_for_you: Notice how strongly visible objects on your desk automatically trigger premotor 'reach-and-use' programs — hiding distracting phones or snacks out of sight saves your frontal 'veto brake' from fighting automatic grabs all day.

jargon_map.plain: neurological condition where one hand performs smooth, purposeful actions (grasping objects or undoing the other hand's work) without the person's conscious intention
jargon_map.analogy: an autopilot co-pilot moving the steering wheel without asking the captain

jargon_map.term: sense of ownership vs sense of agency
jargon_map.plain: knowing 'this arm is part of my body' (ownership) versus feeling 'I consciously commanded that movement' (agency)
jargon_map.analogy: owning the car vs having your foot on the gas pedal

jargon_map.plain: damage to medial frontal Supplementary Motor Area removing the internal brake on automatic object-grasping
jargon_map.analogy: passing a buffet where your hand grabs every roll on sight

jargon_map.plain: damage to the corpus callosum bridge causing the left hand to counteract or undo what the right hand is doing
jargon_map.analogy: right hand buttoning a shirt while left hand unbuttons it

jargon_map.plain: your healthy brain's constant silent vetoing of automatic motor urges triggered whenever eyes see handles, cups, or buttons
jargon_map.analogy: the hidden 'free won't' brake running every second
